message:
I am thinking...: All three instructions decode correctly. The GF2P8AFFINEINVQB with 3 operands, GF2P8MULB with 2 operands, and BNDCL with 2 operands all work.

So the issue isn't with decoding. The PoC IS valid. The problem is that the server's target binary needs to trigger MSAN. Let me re-read the server response:

```
"exit_code":0,"output":"INFO: Seed: 3448618552\nINFO: Loaded 1 modules   (28274 inline 8-bit counters): 28274 [0x124ba38, 0x12528aa), \nINFO: Loaded 1 PC tables (28274 PCs): 28274 [0xed9020,0xf47740), \n/out/fuzz_disasmnext: Running 1 inputs 1 time(s) each.\nRunning: /tmp/poc\nExecuted /tmp/poc in 7 ms\n***\n*** NOTE: fuzzing was not performed, you have only\n***       executed the target code on a fixed set of inputs.\n***\n"
```

It ran the test but exit_code was 0. MSan should have caught the uninitialized read.

Wait - maybe this version of the target uses a "fuzz_disasmnext" which is different from "fuzz_disasm"? The binary is named "fuzz_disasmnext". Let me check if there's a different harness.

Also, looking at the output: the binary at `/out/fuzz_disasmnext` is the MSan-instrumented target. It should detect uninitialized value usage. But it didn't.

Possible explanations:
1. The target binary might be the "next" branch of capstone but possibly a different version where the bug manifests differently
2. My encoding might be triggering a code path where the bug doesn't manifest (e.g., the access value is read but never used in a conditional/branch, so MSan doesn't report it since MSan only reports on "use" not just "read")

MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value when the uninitialized data affects control flow or output. Simply assigning an uninitialized value to a struct field may NOT trigger MSan. The value needs to be USED in a way that matters (e.g., in a branch condition, passed to a system call, etc.).

Looking at the code:
```c
MI->flat_insn->detail->x86.operands[MI->flat_insn->detail->x86.op_count].access = access[MI->flat_insn->detail->x86.op_count];
```

This just stores the uninitialized value into a struct field. MSan won't trigger here. MSan will trigger when that field is later READ and used in a condition.

Looking at the fuzz_disasm.c code after cs_disasm:
```c
for (j = 0; j < count; j++) {
    cs_insn *i = &(all_insn[j]);
    fprintf(outfile, "0x%"PRIx64":\t%s\t\t%s // insn-ID: %u, insn-mnem: %s\n",
           i->address, i->mnemonic, i->op_str, i->id, cs_insn_name(handle, i->id));
    detail = i->detail;
    ...
```

Let me look at what happens with the detail after disassembly in the harness. Does the fuzz harness access the `access` field of operands?
